column7: Found live by FuzzAuthCacheDifferential (FUZZ-GAPS G5) within seconds of its first fuzzing run, not a hand-written seed. setAccountState (internal/core/account_state.go), the shared implementation behind SuspendUser/ReactivateUser/RequirePasswordReset/etc, collected every one of the target user's session AND personal-access-token hashes and evicted them from the HTTP auth cache via customMiddleware.InvalidateTokenCacheByHash for EVERY account-state transition, including a transition INTO plain active (ReactivateUser) -- but InvalidateTokenCacheByHash does not do a plain delete; per its own doc comment it writes a short-lived NEGATIVE tombstone so an in-flight positive validation racing a real revoke can't resurrect a stale entry. Writing that tombstone unconditionally meant a personal access token created WHILE an account is suspended, then swept by that SAME account's later reactivation, was spuriously rejected (401) for up to invalidTokenTTL even though it had never been cached before and the account was already active again -- oracle: the auth decision computed with the cache disagreed with the decision computed with the cache bypassed, for a token neither revoked nor expired. Fixed by scoping the proactive eviction sweep to only run when the TARGET state is more restrictive than plain active (AccountLoginBlocked || AccountRestricted) -- moving toward active never needed a proactive evict for correctness: an over-restrictive stale cache entry is safe (fail-closed), and any EXISTING positive entry already gets AccountState/Restricted refreshed on every hit by serveAuthCacheHit's own re-check, independent of this sweep. Red-before/green-after proving test creates a PAT while suspended, reactivates, and asserts the PAT authenticates on its very first use.
